vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: notion-sync
Version: 2.5.1

The skill provides legitimate Notion synchronization and management capabilities, including reading/writing local markdown files and interacting with the Notion API. It demonstrates good security practices for handling Notion API tokens (avoiding bare CLI arguments). However, the scripts directly use user-provided file paths (e.g., `mdFile`, `localPath`, `outputFile`) for `fs.readFileSync` and `fs.writeFileSync` in `scripts/add-to-database.js`, `scripts/md-to-notion.js`, `scripts/notion-to-md.js`, and `scripts/watch-notion.js`. While this is necessary for the skill's stated purpose, it introduces a vulnerability where an AI agent or user, if tricked, could be instructed to read from or write to arbitrary file paths on the host system, potentially leading to unauthorized data access or modification. This capability, while not inherently malicious, poses a significant risk of abuse, classifying the skill as suspicious.

llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and requested environment access line up with its stated Notion sync purpose — it only needs a Notion token and Node and performs expected file and API operations.

dimensions.detail: Name/description ask for Notion sync and the code and SKILL.md implement search, query, markdown ↔ Notion conversion, updates, batch edits, and watching; required binary (node) and required env var (NOTION_API_KEY) are appropriate for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate on local markdown files, optional state file (memory/notion-watch-state.json), stdin, and the Notion API. These actions are within the scope of bi-directional sync and database management. Note: scripts accept tokens via --token-file, --token-stdin, ~/.notion-token, or NOTION_API_KEY — SKILL.md documents this.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install/download steps are present; the skill is executed as Node scripts requiring Node.js on PATH. No external archives, shorteners, or remote code downloads are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a single credential (Notion integration token) is required, which is proportional. One small mismatch: registry metadata lists NOTION_API_KEY as required, but scripts also accept token files and auto-read ~/.notion-token; this is documented but not declared as a 'required config path'.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled, does not request platform-wide privileges, and does not modify other skills. It reads/writes local files only as expected for syncing and state management.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it needs your Notion integration token and Node.js and will read/write local markdown files, a local watch-state file (by default memory/notion-watch-state.json), and the token file ~/.notion-token if present. Before installing: (1) create a Notion integration with the minimal scopes needed and only share the pages/databases the integration should access; (2) prefer storing the token in a file with restrictive permissions (e.g., ~/.notion-token chmod 600) or pass via stdin rather than exposing it on the command line; (3) review the scripts (they're included) if you want to confirm no additional network endpoints are contacted — the code uses api.notion.com only; (4) be cautious when running batch-update or scripts that modify many pages (use --dry-run first).
